title: How to Switch from Walnut to Storylane
summary: Moving from Walnut to Storylane? This guide covers how to migrate your demos: what happens to existing demos, the steps to switch, and what changes after.
body_markdown:
If you're on Walnut and want to move your demos to Storylane, this guide covers what migration looks like: what happens to your existing demos, the steps to switch, and what changes after.


## Why teams consider Storylane


Here is how the two platforms compare on the points teams usually weigh:


- **P** ublished pricing. Walnut's Ignite plan is $575/month billed annually and includes 3 editor and 3 presenter seats. Sandbox demos are an add-on on Ignite and are included on Accelerate at $1,550/month billed annually (walnut.io/pricing).
- One library. Storylane covers interactive demos, sandbox environments, digital sales rooms, and AI sales agents from one library.
- **Side-by-side detail.** Our[Storylane vs Walnut](https://www.storylane.io/blog/storylane-vs-walnut-io) comparison covers features and pricing in detail.


## What happens to your existing Walnut demos?


Your demos carry over. Share the links with Storylane, the screens get captured and rebuilt as guided steps in your workspace, and a CSM reviews everything with you before it goes live.


## Step-by-step: switching from Walnut to Storylane


**1. Audit your active Walnut demos**


List every demo currently embedded on your site, shared in outbound sequences, or used in sales calls. Prioritize these for migration. Any demo you're actively sending to prospects should be moved first.


**2. Start a Storylane trial or book a migration call**


Sign up at storylane.io or book a demo directly. For teams with multiple active demos, the migration call is faster. Storylane's team handles the heavy lifting and your CSM is assigned from day one.


**3. Send your Walnut demo links**


Share the URLs. Storylane's automation captures your screens and rebuilds the guided steps in your workspace.


**4. Review and improve with your CSM**


Your CSM walks through the migrated demos with you. This is where you add branching, set up[lead capture forms](https://www.storylane.io/blog/lead-forms-in-storylane-capturing-your-most-promising-leads) , enable[viewer identification and CRM routing](https://www.storylane.io/blog/guide-to-lead-attribution-for-interactive-demos) , and adapt any flows that need restructuring for self-serve use.


**5. Replace your embed codes and go live**


Swap the Walnut links for Storylane's. Storylane supports[embedding across your full go-to-market stack](https://www.storylane.io/blog/product-demos-on-multiple-platforms) : website, email sequences, sales decks, LinkedIn outreach, and review sites like G2.


## What you gain after switching


- **Demos that update screen by screen, not flow by flow.** When your product changes, swap the affected screens in Storylane without touching the rest of the demo.
- **Lead capture and CRM routing.** Gate demos with a form or identify viewers without gating. Route step-level engagement directly to HubSpot or Salesforce so your sales team follows up on the right accounts at the right time.
- **One demo, multiple buyer paths.** Build branching flows for different roles, industries, or use cases from a single demo. No more maintaining separate linear flows for each segment your team serves.
- **Interactive demos, sandboxes and sales rooms in one platform.** Interactive demos, sandbox environments, and digital sales rooms all live in Storylane. See storylane.io/plans for what each plan includes.
